FFM introductory note
Presentation on the CNMP, its aims and objectives:
In terms of the Public Prosecutor’s Office handling of cases involving organised criminal groups, do you have any specific aims or objectives?
Could you describe the judicial process of prosecuting members of organised criminal groups?
Can you outline any barriers the public prosecutor’s offices face in the context of prosecuting organised criminal groups?
Can you tell us about the protections available to victims during the judicial process?
Is this assistance open to any victim?
Can the CNMP handle complaints against public prosecutor’s offices on behalf of citizens? If so, can you outline the procedure?
Have you given any specific recommendations regarding victims of organised crime?
We are aware that OCGs were born in and are active in prisons. What have the CNMP recommended to address that?
Would you say this is effective?
Interview with CNMP (National Council of the Public Prosecutor’s Office)
Can you give us an overview of the work the UNODC are doing in Brazil in relation to organised criminal groups?
What do you believe are the main barriers to tackling organised criminal groups in Brazil?
Would you say there is a difference in approach between the Bolsonaro and Lula administrations in tackling organised criminal groups?
Are you aware of any pending legislation or initiatives to tackle organised crime?
Are you aware or able to estimate what percentage of homicides (and / or violent crimes) are attributed to organised crime in Brazil?
Are you able to tell us categories or profiles of ‘typical’ victims of organised crime?
Could you tell us about your work on CRIMJUST? Specifically, how do UNODC work to enhance the capacity of criminal justice actors in practice in relation to organised crime?
Does the UNODC CRIMJUST project work with state/civil police or only federal police?
How does UNODC CRIMJUST work to improve human-rights and gender- based considerations in investigations of organised criminal activity?
Could you tell us about your work on PRIS-COOP?
Who is affected by organised criminal groups and in what way?
Interview with United Nations Office for Drugs and Crime (UNODC)
Background
We’re aware that SENASP develop policies, guidelines, and actions for public security in the country. Please could you give us an overview of key examples in relation to organised crime?
Can you tell us a little more about the types of crimes and statistics you record?
Do you record statistics on detentions and convictions or only arrests?
Do you disaggregate any data or statistics by the actor of the offence?
To what extent do you think that everyday people are affected by serious and organised crime in Brazil?
In which areas are Brazilian nationals most likely to be impacted by the violent impacts of organised criminal groups in Brazil?
Are you aware of any specific groups or profiles of people that OCGs target and for what reason?
Can you share any information on PROVITA?
Interview with The National Secretariat of Public Security (SENASP)
Background
Can you give us a brief overview of how the police system in Brazil is organised and structured?
What are the main roles and responsibilities of the immigration department?
Can you tell us about the work you do in relation to monitoring the travel patterns of Brazilian citizens leaving the country for purposes of organised crime?
Could you explain how this work impacts on crime committed within Brazil?

When deciding an asylum claim, a consideration is made to whether or not someone could relocate internally within a country in order to escape whatever risk they’re facing. If someone was to move within Brazil, are there any processes they need to go through when they arrive, for example registering with the local authorities etc?
Interview with Federal Police, Immigration Department
Background
Can you tell us about the work you’re doing to combat serious and organised crime in Brazil?
What are the main challenges you experience when it comes to dealing with organised crime at the federal level?
How big is the criminal population in relation to the general population?
To what extent do you think that everyday people are affected by organised criminal groups in Brazil?
Are you aware of any specific groups or profiles of people that OCGs target and for what reason?
Could you tell us more about the federal prison system?
In your opinion, could someone affected by OCG activity relocate to another part of Brazil to avoid the gang?
Can you tell us about the witness protection programme?
Would family also be protected or is it only the direct witness?
Do the PCC or CV target any particular demographic?
Would someone be able to internally relocate in Brazil to escape an organised criminal group?
If a person who was working with them wanted to leave, would they be at risk?
Would someone be able to receive protection from the police against OCGs?
What is the threshold for risk – is anyone who speaks out against the OCGs in danger?
What kind of infraction would make the PCC or CV want to track someone across the country?
If someone owed money, would they be a target that got followed?
Do the PCC or CV target any particular demographic for the purposes of recruitment?
These people who are bribed or corrupted, do the gang then count them as part of the organisation, or are they able to stop working for them?
Where is corruption most prevalent?
Interview with Federal Police of Brazil, Serious and Organised Crime Division
We are aware that there has been congressional discussion around organised crime – please can you describe your involvement in combatting organised criminal groups?
Could you tell us if there is any pending legislation or policy on tackling organised criminal groups in Brazil?
Is there a specific profile of persons who are involved with gangs or organised criminal groups?
Do OCGs approach people to recruit them or do people approach the groups to join?
Is corruption common across Brazil?
What would happen if someone was approached by an organised criminal gang and that person refused to cooperate/work with them?
If someone was part of an organised criminal group and wanted to leave, would they be able to?
Would somebody be able to internally relocate within Brazil in order to escape the threat of an organised criminal group?
If somebody was a member of the PCC in Sao Paulo but then left, would the PCC be able to track them? If so, what sort of profile would they need to have for the PCC to want to track them?
Do different factions of the same organised group communicate with each other?
Are protections available for victims of organised crime, or only witnesses?
Is there are particular person or group that would be most at risk of being targeted by the PCC or CV, who they would actively want to harm?
Interview with Legislative Consultants of the Chamber of Deputies
Please could you tell us about the specific areas of work your organisation does in relation to organised criminal groups in Brazil?
Does the Witness Protection Program protect only witnesses or also their family?
Is it in the nature of the PCC or CV to target family members?
Please could you tell us more about what life is like for people living in areas controlled by organised criminal groups?
Is there a particular group or demographic (relating to age, gender, ethnicity, job role) of person who would be targeted by the PCC or the CV?
Would you say these OCGs actively recruit or do they have enough willing participants?
If a teen boy decided to start working for an OCG, would he later be able to leave the group?
Would he suffer retribution for this?
What about when they’re higher in the group?
If either of these groups approached someone they wanted in their organisation, could the person say no?
We heard about the PCC sponsoring students to go to university. Could those people leave the group?
If someone had a debt, and they moved say from Rio de Janeiro to somewhere North, would the PCC have the means or desire to track them?
What sort of figure is a large debt?
Generally, are people less likely to be pursued for smaller debts?
What kind of infraction would cause an armed gang to pursue someone? What would warrant what response?
Are there standard punishments in the informal tribunals?
Could you tell us about militias and how they fit into the landscape of armed groups?
What are the goals of the militias?
Not drug trafficking?
To what extent are the state effective in combatting organised criminal groups?
If someone owed money to an OCG and were threatened, what would happen if they went to police?
If someone was threatened because of flirting with a gang member’s partner, would the police help then?
Are there any other forms of support available to people threatened by gangs, for example NGOs?
Are militias present elsewhere in Brazil?
Is the state effective in combatting corruption? Is there an appetite to bring corrupt people to justice?
Interview with Grupo de Novos Ilegalismos da Universidade Federale Fluminense (GENI/UFF)
Can you tell me about your organisation and the work that you do?
Do you do any work which is specifically related to gangs or organised criminal groups?
Can you tell me some of the ways in which people’s everyday lives are affected by gangs/criminal groups?
Are there any people who are particularly at risk of harm from gangs/organised criminal groups? For example relating to their age, gender, ethnicity, socio- economic group?
Can you tell me some of the reasons why gangs would target an individual?
Can you tell us anything about how gangs recruit people? Do they target any particular types of person? Relating for example to age, gender, ethnicity?
Interview with Rio de Paz
Can you tell me about your organisation and the work that you do?
We understand that the PCC are the main organised criminal group that operates in Sao Paulo. Can you tell us about how they operate? Do they operate throughout the city or only in favelas?
Can you tell me some of the ways in which people’s everyday lives are affected by the PCC?
Are there any people who are particularly at risk of harm from the PCC? For example relating to age, gender, ethnicity, socio-economic group?
Regarding the example of the PCC becoming involved in municipal elections: are there any anti-corruption measures in place to stop this from happening?
Are there police militias in Sao Paulo or just the PCC?
Interview with Instituto Sou da Paz
Please could you tell us about the specific areas of work your organisation does in relation to organised criminal groups in Brazil?
How effective are federal prisons in disrupting the gangs?
Is there a particular group or demographic (such as age, gender, ethnicity, job role) of person who would be targeted or recruited by the PCC?
Could someone leave the PCC after being a part of the group?
If someone had a debt, and they moved from Sao Paulo to elsewhere, would the PCC have the means or desire to track them?
What would happen if someone refused to join the group?
Could you tell us more about their ethical code - what happens if someone commits an infraction?
If someone broke one of the PCC’s rules, what would happen?
What infraction would result in death or serious punishment?
A lot of people claim they fear the PCC because they owe them money. Would this put someone at risk of serious harm?
To what extent are the state independent and effective in combatting and prosecuting members of the PCC?
If, for example, someone went to the police and said they had been threatened by an organised criminal group because they owed them money, what would happen?
Would the PCC target the families of those they are interested in?
Are people able to receive any form of help or protection from NGOs?
How effective is the Witness Protection Programe?
Are there limits to who can be part of the Witness Protection Programme?
In prisons controlled by the PCC, would an inmate have to join them?
In communities controlled by the PCC, do people need to abide by their rules?
Can anyone access their mediation system?
How much territory is controlled by PCC in Sao Paulo?
You said they’d have to go to a brother first. What would happen if someone called the police?
How pervasively is the PCC extending into state or public bodies?
Interview with Centre for the Study of Violence (NEV-USP)
We’re aware the PCC has diversified its operations and become very organised and sophisticated over the years. How have they diversified, become more organised and sophisticated?
To what extent are every day citizens affected by their operations?
Could you tell us more about the PCC acting as law enforcement in these communities?
How do the PCC enforce their rules?
What kind of infraction would result in being killed?
If someone borrowed money from the PCC and didn’t pay it back, what would the punishment be?
Does the amount of debt someone owes make a difference to the punishment they face?
If someone owed money and didn’t pay, could they escape to another part of Brazil?
Do the PCC often also target the family members of those they’re targeting?
What would happen if someone went to the state police and said they were being threatened by the PCC?
Are people allowed to leave the gang? Are there conditions to this? Does it differ based on the person’s profile?
Could you explain to us the burden of proof in Brazil; how much evidence is needed to successfully prosecute members of OCGs?
We’re keen to understand how many members of OCGs are arrested and convicted each year in Brazil. Could you share any statistics with us on this?
Could you tell us how many OCG members are prosecuted each year?
Interview with Prosecutor Lincoln Gakiya
Background
What profile of people do you feel are genuinely at risk from OCGs?
Could you tell us more about some of the rules imposed on people in these communities?
Are the punishments standardised or are they arbitrary? Do they change with each instance?
Is that the PROVITA programme?
Could you tell us about any more challenges you face in investigating crimes committed by the PCC?
Was he found guilty or innocent?
Why did they make that decision?
Do you work much with the federal police or state police in other states in Brazil?
Do you have statistics on arrests and detentions of OCG members?
Would someone fearing the PCC in Sao Paulo be able to internally relocate to escape that risk?
Would there be any circumstances where the PCC would wish to pursue someone who internally relocated?
Interview with Criminal Investigation Department of the Sao Paulo Civil Police
Background
What are some of the challenges facing law enforcement when it comes to combatting organised criminal groups?
If someone is charged with a crime, how much time usually passes between the charge and sentencing?
Are members of the judiciary ever subjected to intimidation?

We’ve heard that in the federal prison system inmates can pass information through their lawyers to people outside of the prison. Is there anything being done to change or prevent that from happening?
How does the federal police interact with the state police?
You mentioned corruption within the state police. How does Brazil attempt to combat corruption?
What happens when a member of the state police is found to be corrupt and/or working with an organised criminal group?
Is it common that corrupt police get brought to justice?
Are there any oversight mechanisms of the judiciary?
Interview with Federal Police of Brazil, São Paulo
Interview notes
